title: Explaining Higher Differential-Linear Correlations
summary: Experiments sometimes find absolute correlations above theory, improving attack efficiency; explaining the discrepancy and determining whether linear-hull effects cause the excess remains open.

formal_statement.body: Experimental verification of the differential-linear attacks sometimes yields absolute correlations higher than their theoretical estimates, making the attacks more efficient than estimated. The open problem is to explain this theory--experiment discrepancy and determine whether linear-hull effects cause the unexpectedly high absolute correlations.

scope.domain: Differential-linear cryptanalysis and linear-hull effects in symmetric ciphers.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Explain the discrepancy between observed and theoretical absolute correlations and determine whether linear-hull effects cause the unexpectedly high values.

citations.label: Improved Differential-Linear Attacks with Applications to ARX Ciphers

progress.summary: The source reports that experimental verification sometimes produces higher-than-expected absolute correlations, making the attacks more efficient than estimated. It explicitly presents explaining these deviations and assessing likely linear-hull effects as a question to tackle.
citation_labels: Christof Beierle et al., Improved Differential-Linear Attacks with Applications to ARX Ciphers
